mainTopic: A chain of רב's aggadic sayings (the בית הכנסת's height, dangers and sufferings, the dream fast), when Torah learners stop for קריאת שמע and תפלה, and a new משנה on safeguards before and on שבת.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a calculation about סדום, landing on 26 calm years and proving it from a פסוק. It then brings a chain of sayings from רב, all passed down by רבא בר מחסיא through רב חמא בר גוריא. A city whose houses are taller than its בית הכנסת will be destroyed, though poles and towers do not count. רב אשי says this is how he saved מתא מחסיא, and when the city falls anyway, the גמרא answers that it fell for a different sin. Next come a ranking of whose power is most dangerous to live under, a list of the worst kinds of suffering, and a saying that a government's concerns are too vast to write down. Then רב teaches that a fast cancels a bad dream; רב חסדא adds that it must be on the same day, and רב יוסף adds that it applies even on שבת. A story about רב יהושע בריה דרב אידי shows why a dream fast cannot be postponed. The גמרא returns to the משנה on stopping for קריאת שמע and תפלה, and sorts out three cases: ordinary people, full-time learners like רבי שמעון בן יוחי, and those doing עיבור השנה. Finally, a new משנה lists safeguards against slipping into a שבת violation out of habit, and the גמרא begins by quoting a related משנה about drinking across two domains.

steps.title: Finishing the count for סדום: twenty-six years, proven from a verse
steps.stepSummary: This amud picks up in the middle of a calculation about the years of סדום. It reaches the number 26 and brings the פסוק about the kings serving and rebelling against כדרלעומר as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Twenty-six, as it is written: 'Twelve years they served כדרלעומר, and thirteen years they rebelled, and in the fourteenth year...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a calculation from the previous page about the years of סדום. It shows where the number 26 comes from by quoting a פסוק in בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק counts twelve years of serving כדרלעומר and then a war in the fourteenth year. According to the explanation the גמרא is building on, those 12 and 14 years were not quiet, peaceful years. Taking them away from the total leaves the 26 calm years in which סדום sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written; introduces a פסוק as the source
Chedorlaomer, the king whom סדום and its neighbors served (בראשית יד)
And so on; the verse continues

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this amud starts a new topic here. These words are the tail end of a sentence from the previous page. The number 26 is the answer to a calculation that started there.

phrases.english: Twenty-six, as it is written:
phrases.notes: The end of the calculation from the previous page.

phrases.english: "Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer
and thirteen years they rebelled.
And in the fourteenth year, etc."
phrases.notes: In the fourteenth year כדרלעומר came to make war.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes a calculation that began on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That the calm years of סדום in which it sinned came to 26.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית יד:ד-ה, which counts twelve years of service and a war in the fourteenth year.

steps.title: A city with roofs higher than the synagogue will be destroyed
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that any city whose roofs are taller than its בית הכנסת will end up destroyed. He hints to this from a פסוק in עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא בר מחסיא said that רב חמא בר גוריא said that רב said: Any city whose roofs are higher than the בית הכנסת will in the end be destroyed. As it says: 'To raise up the house of our God and to restore its ruins.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רב: a city that builds its houses taller than its בית הכנסת will eventually be ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making ordinary houses taller than the house of תפילה shows disrespect for the בית הכנסת. The פסוק puts 'raising up the house of our God' right next to 'its ruins.' This hints that failing to raise up God's house leads to ruin.

keyTerms.meaning: In the end it will be destroyed

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the source for the practice that a בית הכנסת should be the tallest building in town.

phrases.english: And Rava bar Mechasya said
phrases.notes: The same chain of names introduces a whole series of teachings.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עִיר שֶׁגַּגּוֹתֶיהָ גְּבוֹהִין מִבֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
phrases.english: Any city whose roofs are higher than the synagogue
will in the end be destroyed.
As it is said: "To raise up the house of our God
and to restore its ruins."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא בַּר מַחְסֵיָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching in the chain of רב's statements. It is not connected to the topic of סדום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A city whose houses are taller than its בית הכנסת is destined for destruction.

steps.title: The rule covers the houses themselves, not poles and towers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב's rule. It applies only when the actual houses are taller. Poles or towers sticking up from the houses do not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only to houses. But poles and towers, we have no problem with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a limit on the rule it just taught, explaining exactly what counts as 'higher than the בית הכנסת.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the main building of a house is measured. Thin decorative or functional additions above the roof, like poles and towers, are not counted. So they do not bring on the danger.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply only to; introduces a limit on a rule
Poles or posts sticking up from a building
Towers or turrets on top of a building
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: And this applies only to houses,
but with poles and towers,
we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This narrows the rule in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the height of the houses themselves is compared to the בית הכנסת. Poles and towers are not included.

steps.title: רב אשי says he saved מתא מחסיא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that he made sure מתא מחסיא would not be destroyed. He did this by keeping its בית הכנסת taller than the houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I made it so that מתא מחסיא would not be destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tells how he put רב's rule into practice in his own city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי built the בית הכנסת of מתא מחסיא taller than every other building. He claims that by doing so he protected the city from the destruction רב warned about. This statement sets up the challenge that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: I made it so, I caused
The town where רב אשי ran his ישיבה

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I caused Mata Mechasya
not to be destroyed.
phrases.notes: He did this by building the בית הכנסת taller than the houses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a real-life use of רב's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Building the בית הכנסת tall protected מתא מחסיא from this particular kind of destruction.

steps.title: But the city was destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי: מתא מחסיא was eventually destroyed anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was destroyed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to רב אשי's claim, because history shows that מתא מחסיא was in fact destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tall בית הכנסת was supposed to protect the city, then its destruction seems to prove that the protection did not work. That would make רב אשי's claim look false.

keyTerms.meaning: But look; opens a challenge from known facts

phrases.english: But it was destroyed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This attacks רב אשי's claim in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that he saved מתא מחסיא from destruction.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The city was destroyed in the end, which seems to contradict the claim that it was protected.

steps.title: It was not destroyed for that sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that מתא מחסיא was destroyed because of other sins, not because of the height of the houses.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was not destroyed because of that sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the city was destroyed, but for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי only protected the city from the punishment for disrespecting the בית הכנסת. A tall בית הכנסת does not shield a city from punishment for other sins. So רב אשי's claim still holds.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule: houses must not be taller than the בית הכנסת, but poles and towers do not count. Following the rule removes this one cause of destruction, not every cause.

phrases.english: It was not destroyed because of that sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the claim: the protection covered only one specific sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A tall בית הכנסת guarantees that the city will never be destroyed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A tall בית הכנסת prevents only the destruction caused by disrespecting it. The city fell because of other sins.

steps.title: Whose power is hardest to live under
steps.stepSummary: רב ranks whose rule is harder to bear: ישמעאל, a נכרי, a חבר, a תלמיד חכם, and hardest of all, an orphan and a widow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא בר מחסיא said that רב חמא בר גוריא said that רב said: Better under ישמעאל than under a נכרי. Better under a נכרי than under a חבר. Better under a חבר than under a תלמיד חכם. Better under a תלמיד חכם than under an orphan and a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching from רב ranks how dangerous it is to be under the power of different kinds of people. Each one is worse than the one before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list moves from harsh foreign rulers to people whose power comes from Heaven. ישמעאל is easier to live under than a נכרי, which the reference translation explains as the Romans. A נכרי is easier than a חבר, a Persian fire priest. Hurting a תלמיד חכם brings punishment from Heaven. Hurting an orphan or a widow is worst of all, because ה' promised to hear their cries.

keyTerms.meaning: Under; under the rule or power of
A stranger; explained in the reference translation as the Romans

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the list as ranking how good or bad these people are. It ranks how dangerous it is to be in a position where you might wrong them.

phrases.english: And Rava bar Mechasya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
Under Yishmael and not under a stranger.
Under a stranger and not under a Chabar.
phrases.notes: A חבר is a Persian fire priest.

phrases.aramaic: תַּחַת חַבָּר וְלֹא תַּחַת תַּלְמִיד חָכָם.
phrases.english: Under a Chabar and not under a Torah scholar.

phrases.aramaic: תַּחַת תַּלְמִיד חָכָם וְלֹא תַּחַת יָתוֹם וְאַלְמָנָה.
phrases.english: Under a Torah scholar and not under an orphan and a widow.
phrases.notes: ה' promised to hear their cries (שמות כב).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא בַּר מַחְסֵיָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב: תַּחַת יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next teaching in the chain of רב's statements. It is a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The more Heaven defends a person, the more dangerous it is to be under their power, where you might come to wrong them. An orphan and a widow are at the top of that list.

steps.title: The worst kinds of suffering
steps.stepSummary: רב lists the worst kind within each type of suffering: intestinal illness, heart pain, headache, and a bad wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא בר מחסיא said that רב חמא בר גוריא said that רב said: Any illness, but not intestinal illness. Any pain, but not heart pain. Any ache, but not a headache. Any evil, but not an evil wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The next teaching in the chain is a list from רב. In each category of suffering, he names the one kind that is worse than all the others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line follows the same pattern: 'any ___, but not ___.' A person would rather suffer any other illness than an intestinal one, and any other pain than heart pain. The same goes for headaches among aches, and a bad wife among all troubles.

phrases.english: And Rava bar Mechasya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
Any illness, but not intestinal illness.
Any pain, but not heart pain.
Any ache, but not a headache.
Any evil, but not an evil wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא בַּר מַחְסֵיָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב: כׇּל חוֹלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next teaching in the chain of רב's statements. It is a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Within each kind of suffering, one is the hardest: intestinal illness, heart pain, headache, and a bad wife.

steps.title: Government's concerns are too vast to write down
steps.stepSummary: רב says that even if all the seas were ink and all people were scribes, they could not write out everything a government must deal with.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא בר מחסיא said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא in the name of רב: If all the seas were ink, the swamp reeds were pens, the heavens were parchment, and all people were scribes, they still could not write out the full scope of government.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another saying from the same chain of rabbis. This one is about how huge the responsibilities of a ruler are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of earlier steps about rulers and authority. The point is that a government deals with endless issues, far more than anyone could ever list.

keyTerms.meaning: Pens or quills, here made from reeds
The full 'space' or scope of government

phrases.english: And Rava bar Meḥasseya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
If all the seas were ink,
and the swamp reeds were quills,
and the heavens were parchment,
and all people were scribes —
they would not be enough to write
the full scope of government.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא בַּר מַחְסֵיָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another saying in the same chain of transmission, continuing the theme of rulers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concerns of government are beyond measure.

steps.title: A verse that hints at this idea
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא finds a פסוק in משלי showing that the heart of kings cannot be searched out.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the פסוק for this? רב משרשיא said: 'The heavens for height, the earth for depth, and the heart of kings cannot be searched out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source in the תנ"ך for רב's idea. רב משרשיא brings a פסוק from משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the heart of kings next to the height of the sky and the depth of the earth. All three are beyond human measure, which matches רב's picture of endless writing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse (that hints at this)?
Cannot be searched out or measured

phrases.english: What is the verse?
Rav Mesharshiya said:
"The heavens for height and the earth for depth,
and the heart of kings is unsearchable" (Proverbs 25:3).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a verse supporting רב's statement
steps.raayaObject: רב's statement that government's concerns cannot be measured

steps.title: Fasting cancels a bad dream
steps.stepSummary: רב says a fast works against a bad dream the way fire burns straw.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא בר מחסיא said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא in the name of רב: A fast is good against a dream, like fire against straw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new saying from the same chain of rabbis. This one is about fasting after a bad dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fire burns straw quickly and completely. Likewise, a fast is a strong and effective way to cancel the bad meaning of a dream.

keyTerms.meaning: Chaff or straw, which burns very easily

phrases.english: And Rava bar Meḥasseya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
A fast is effective for a dream
like fire for chaff.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא בַּר מַחְסֵיָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new saying in the same chain, on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fasting is highly effective at cancelling a bad dream.

steps.title: The fast must be on the same day
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds that the fast works only if it is done on the day of the dream.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: And on that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a condition to רב's rule about fasting for a dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fast works only if it is kept on the very day of the dream, not on a later day. This condition is exactly what the story in steps 14-16 depends on.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: And on that same day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a timing condition to רב's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dream fast is effective on the day of the dream.

steps.title: A dream fast is allowed even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds that one may fast for a bad dream even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: Even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds that this kind of fast is allowed even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one does not fast on שבת. Since the dream fast must be done that same day, it is allowed even when that day is שבת.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: Even on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the same-day rule even to שבת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may fast for a bad dream even on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: A dream fast is very effective, must be on the day of the dream, and is allowed even on שבת.

steps.title: A guest refuses a fine meal because he is fasting
steps.stepSummary: רב יהושע בריה דרב אידי visits רב אשי. His hosts prepare a special calf, but he tells them he is fasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהושע the son of רב אידי came to רב אשי's house. They prepared a third-born calf for him. They said: Let the master taste something. He said: I am fasting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story. It sets up a question about why the guest will not eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hosts went out of their way with a top-quality calf. His refusal raises the obvious question of why he could not simply delay his fast.

keyTerms.meaning: A third-born calf, whose meat is especially good
I am sitting in a fast

phrases.english: Rav Yehoshua, son of Rav Idi,
happened to come to the house of Rav Ashi.
They prepared a third-born calf for him.
They said to him: Let the Master taste something.
He said to them: I am in the middle of a fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידֵּי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that illustrates the dream-fast rules
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהושע would not eat because he was fasting.

steps.title: Why not postpone the fast?
steps.stepSummary: The hosts challenge him with רב יהודה's rule that a person may 'borrow' a fast and pay it back on another day.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Doesn't the master hold like רב יהודה? רב יהודה said: A person may borrow his fast and repay it.
steps.whatsHappening: The hosts push back. They say he could postpone his fast and eat with them now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יהודה, a fast you took on yourself can be moved to another day. That should let him eat now and fast later.

keyTerms.meaning: A person may borrow his fast and repay it later

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וְלָא סָבַר לֵיהּ מָר
phrases.english: They said to him: Doesn't the Master hold
like this ruling of Rav Yehuda?
For Rav Yehuda said:
A person may borrow his fast and repay it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא סָבַר לֵיהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the guest's refusal to eat
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהושע's insistence on fasting that day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fasts can be postponed according to רב יהודה, so he has no need to refuse the meal.

steps.title: A dream fast cannot be postponed
steps.stepSummary: He answers that this is a fast for a dream, which must be done on the same day, and quotes רב, רב חסדא, and רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: It is a fast for a dream. And רב said: A fast is good against a dream like fire against straw. And רב חסדא said: On that same day. And רב יוסף said: Even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The guest explains that a dream fast is different. He repeats the same sayings we just learned to prove his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's rule applies to ordinary fasts. A dream fast only works on the day of the dream, as רב חסדא said, so it cannot be pushed off. The sayings are repeated here on purpose: now they serve as proof inside the story.

keyTerms.meaning: A fast for a bad dream

steps.confusionAlert: The repeated quotes are not a copying mistake. The גמרא repeats them because they are now used as the guest's proof.

phrases.english: He said to them: It is a fast for a dream.
And Rava bar Meḥasseya said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
A fast is effective for a dream like fire for chaff.
And Rav Ḥisda said: And on that same day.
And Rav Yosef said: Even on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hosts' challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a dream fast is an exception to the postponement rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every fast can be borrowed and repaid later.
steps.terutzMaskana: A dream fast must be on the same day, so it cannot be postponed.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's rule about postponing a fast does not apply to a dream fast, which must be kept on the day of the dream.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: stopping for קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if they already started, they need not stop, but they do stop for קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they already began, they do not stop. They do stop for קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its words. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (on 9b) discussed activities like a haircut or a meal begun near the time for תפלה. Once started, one may finish before praying, but one must stop for קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: And if they began, they do not stop;
they stop for the recitation of Shema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic sayings and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once started, one need not stop for תפלה, but must stop for קריאת שמע.

steps.title: Why does the משנה repeat itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the beginning of the משנה already said 'they do not stop,' so why say it again?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first part of the משנה already taught 'they do not stop'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an apparent repetition in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה does not repeat itself for no reason. The full סיפא of the משנה on 9b ends 'ואין מפסיקין לתפלה', meaning they do not stop for תפלה. The רישא already said 'ואם התחילו אין מפסיקין', so this ending seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה

phrases.english: Didn't the first clause already teach
'they do not stop'?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ רֵישָׁא אֵין מַפְסִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The repeated phrase 'אין מפסיקין' in the סיפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It was already stated in the רישא, so repeating it seems pointless.

steps.title: The end of the משנה is about Torah learners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the סיפא is talking about a new case: people learning תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The latter part comes to teach about words of תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the סיפא is not a repeat. It is about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא was about ordinary activities like a haircut or a meal. The סיפא teaches about people learning תורה: they need not stop for תפלה, but must stop for קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part of the משנה
We have come to (a new topic)

phrases.english: In the latter clause we have come to matters of Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy question
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case: the סיפא deals with a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא merely repeats the רישא about ordinary activities.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא is about people learning תורה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about Torah learners
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that scholars learning תורה stop for קריאת שמע but not for תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Scholars who were learning תורה stop for קריאת שמע, and do not stop for תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up its reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states exactly the rule the גמרא found in the סיפא. This shows that Torah learners really do have this rule.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
Scholars who were engaged in Torah study —
stop for the recitation of Shema,
and do not stop for prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer that the סיפא is about Torah learners
steps.raayaObject: The claim that Torah learners stop for קריאת שמע but not for תפלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about חברים engaged in Torah study

steps.title: Only full-time learners may skip stopping for prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ברייתא's rule applies only to people like רבי שמעון בן יוחי, whose תורה is their whole occupation. People like us stop for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This was taught only about people like רבי שמעון בן יוחי and his colleagues, whose תורה is their occupation. But people like us stop for both קריאת שמע and תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן narrows the rule of the ברייתא to a special group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only those who learn full-time and never stop for work may skip interrupting for תפלה. Ordinary learners, who stop for other things anyway, must stop for both קריאת שמע and תפלה.
steps.whatToRemember: Torah learners stop for קריאת שמע. Only full-time learners like רבי שמעון בן יוחי are excused from stopping for תפלה; everyone else stops for both.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: the exemption from stopping for תפלה belongs to a rare level of full-time devotion, not to every learner.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They taught this only regarding the likes of
Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai and his colleagues,
whose Torah is their occupation.
But the likes of us
stop for the recitation of Shema and for prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's exemption from stopping for תפלה to full-time learners
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only those whose תורה is their occupation are exempt from stopping for תפלה; ordinary people stop for both.

steps.title: A ברייתא says scholars do not stop even for קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says learners do not stop for קריאת שמע, which goes against the ברייתא from step 20.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: Just as they do not stop for תפלה, so too they do not stop for קריאת שמע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from step 20, which said learners stop for קריאת שמע. Here is another ברייתא that says they do not stop for it at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said learners stop for קריאת שמע but not for תפלה. This new ברייתא treats both the same and says they stop for neither. The two ברייתות seem to contradict each other.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Just as they do not stop for prayer,
so too they do not stop for Shema!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 20 with a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in step 20 that says learners stop for קריאת שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא says learners stop for neither קריאת שמע nor תפלה, so the two sources clash.

steps.title: That ברייתא is about people working on the leap year
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא is talking about people busy with עיבור השנה, not ordinary learners.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about people busy with making the leap year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The ברייתא that says 'do not stop even for קריאת שמע' is about a special group: the חכמים deciding עיבור השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות are not talking about the same people. Ordinary learners stop for קריאת שמע. Those doing עיבור השנה do not stop at all, because the whole calendar and all the ימים טובים depend on their work.

keyTerms.meaning: Adding a month to make a leap year

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a third level of תורה learning. It is a special communal task, setting the calendar, and that is why it gets its own rule.

phrases.english: When that was taught — it was regarding intercalation of the year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different case (אוקימתא): each ברייתא refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות speak about ordinary learners and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second ברייתא speaks only about those doing עיבור השנה, who stop for neither.

steps.title: Proof: in יבנה they did not stop during the leap-year work
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק reports that when they worked on עיבור השנה in יבנה, they stopped for neither קריאת שמע nor תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אדא בר אהבה said, and the elders of הגרוניא also taught: רבי אלעזר בר צדוק said, 'When we were busy with עיבור השנה in יבנה, we did not stop for קריאת שמע or for תפלה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for its answer. An eyewitness report from יבנה shows that those doing עיבור השנה did not stop at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 claimed the 'do not stop for anything' rule fits עיבור השנה. Here רבי אלעזר בר צדוק says exactly that from personal experience. So the answer has real support.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders of the town of הגרוניא
יבנה, the seat of the סנהדרין after the חורבן

steps.whatToRemember: Three different cases: ordinary people stop for both קריאת שמע and תפלה. Those whose תורה is their full-time occupation, like רבי שמעון בן יוחי, stop only for קריאת שמע. Those doing עיבור השנה, a special communal task, stop for neither.

phrases.english: As Rav Adda bar Ahava said,
and so too the elders of Hagronya taught:
Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok said:
When we were engaged in intercalating the year in Yavne,
we would not stop,
neither for Shema nor for prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'do not stop even for קריאת שמע' rule belongs to עיבור השנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The report of רבי אלעזר בר צדוק about יבנה, passed on by רב אדא בר אהבה and the elders of הגרוניא.

steps.title: New משנה: safeguards before and on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A tailor should not go out with his needle, or a scribe with his quill, close to nightfall. One should not check clothes or read by candlelight on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A tailor should not go out with his needle close to nightfall, in case he forgets and goes out with it after שבת starts. A scribe should not go out with his quill. One should not check his clothes for lice, and one should not read by the light of a candle.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists גזירות, protective rules, that keep a person from slipping into a real שבת violation out of habit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A craftsman often carries his tool without thinking. Near nightfall he might keep it on himself into שבת and carry it outside. Checking clothes or reading by candlelight could lead a person to tilt the lamp to get more light, which is a מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: By the light of a lamp

steps.confusionAlert: Carrying a needle on Friday afternoon is not itself forbidden. The concern is only that he might forget it is on him once שבת arrives.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֵצֵא הַחַיָּיט בְּמַחֲטוֹ סָמוּךְ לַחֲשֵׁכָה,
phrases.english: The tailor may not go out with his needle close to nightfall,
lest he forget and go out (with it on Shabbat).
Nor the scribe with his quill.
And one may not search his clothes for lice,
phrases.notes: According to רש"י, this also means by candlelight, like the next clause.

phrases.english: and one may not read by the light of a lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יֵצֵא הַחַיָּיט בְּמַחֲטוֹ סָמוּךְ לַחֲשֵׁכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rabbinic safeguards: no going out with one's work tool near nightfall, and no checking clothes or reading by candlelight on שבת.

steps.title: משנה continued: the חזן, and the זב and זבה
steps.stepSummary: A חזן may look to see where the children are reading by candlelight, but he himself may not read. Similarly, a זב may not eat with a זבה, so they do not become used to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: In truth they said: the חזן may look where the children are reading, but he himself may not read. Similar to this: a זב may not eat with a זבה, because it can lead to the habit of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a limited exception to the candlelight rule. It then adds a similar safeguard from a different area of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Glancing to find the children's place is brief, so it is allowed. Reading on his own could absorb him, and then he might adjust the lamp. A זב and זבה are both טמא, so impurity is not the problem. The concern is that eating together could lead them to forbidden closeness.

keyTerms.meaning: In truth they said (introduces a firm, established rule)
A man or woman with a discharge that causes טומאה

steps.whyThisMatters: The theme that ties the whole משנה together is גזירות against habit leading to sin. The גמרא will now explore this theme.

phrases.english: In truth they said:
the attendant may see where the children are reading,
but he himself may not read.
Similar to this:
the zav may not eat with the zava,
because of becoming accustomed to sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with an exception to the candlelight rule and a parallel safeguard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזן may glance but not read. A זב and זבה may not eat together, because of הרגל עבירה.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes a משנה about drinking across two domains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a משנה from elsewhere: a person should not stand in one domain and drink in the other, unless his head and most of his body are where he drinks.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: A person may not stand in רשות היחיד and drink in רשות הרבים, or stand in רשות הרבים and drink in רשות היחיד. But if he brought his head and most of his body into the place where he is drinking, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes a related משנה, also about a protective rule, so it can ask a question about it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that he might pull the cup back into the domain where he is standing, which would be carrying between domains. Once his head and most of his body are in the drinking area, he and the cup are in the same place, so the worry disappears. This matches our משנה's theme of safeguards against slipping into a violation.

keyTerms.meaning: His head and most of his body

phrases.english: GEMARA:
We learned there (in another mishna):
A person may not stand in the private domain
and drink in the public domain,
(nor stand) in the public domain and drink in the private domain.
But if he brought his head and most of his body
into the place where he is drinking — it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on our משנה by bringing a parallel משנה about a protective rule. It sets up the question that comes next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not drink across the boundary between רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים, unless his head and most of his body are in the drinking domain.
